title: Elias plays the tournament
topic: A chess player named Elias plays a tournament game: a knight sacrifice, a long think by the opponent, an arbiter at the next table, the opponent resigns after forty moves
tail_E: After the final round Elias is the new tournament
target_note: 'champion' is the natural completion of 'is the new tournament' in a context where Elias plays a tournament, his opponent resigns and he leaves the hall as the winner; the word does not occur in the units or the tail, and neither do its German equivalents 'Meister' / 'Champion' (unit 10 uses 'winner' / 'Sieger', a different word). ' champion' is a single Pythia token (id 16928). Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only): p(' champion') = 0.53 on the all-English rendering, rank 1 (next: ' winner' 0.20). A pawn-promotion tail ('... reaches the eighth rank and becomes a' -> queen) was tried first and rejected because pythia-160m ranks ' queen' only 6th there.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (DEV02A, chess player Elias, development family)
notes: Development family (dose/threshold choice only, never for confirmation). Ten units: Elias plays his first tournament game; the opponent moves a pawn after a long pause; the spectators follow the game on a screen; Elias sacrifices a knight; the other player thinks for twenty minutes; the position becomes sharp after the exchange; an arbiter checks the scoresheets at the next table; Elias finds a strong rook move; the opponent resigns after forty moves; Elias leaves the hall as the winner. Subjects alternate between the protagonist (Elias), other people (his opponent, the other player, an arbiter, the spectators - plural) and objects (the position), so that C3 switches cross singular and plural subject-verb agreement. Unit 6 uses the reflexive 'verschärft sich' instead of 'wird sehr scharf' so that the adjunct does not have to follow a closed verb bracket; unit 9 uses 'kapituliert' (chess reporting usage) instead of the separable 'gibt auf'. No separable verbs. Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Units 1 and 10 read naturally in English, unit 9 in German; unit 10 closes the scene.
